Final rebar-debug report

Problem: `tests/unit/test_build_provenance.py::test_install_from_sdist_preserves_commit` deterministically emitted Python’s future-default tar extraction warning.

Proven root cause: `tests/unit/test_build_provenance.py:146` reached CPython 3.12.13 `TarFile._get_filter_function(None)` because the extractall call omitted `filter=` and no class extraction filter was configured. That exact runtime branch emitted the warning before extraction.

Proof: promoting DeprecationWarning to an error reproduced the failure. Installing `tarfile.data_filter` as the runtime default while leaving the test unchanged made the same scenario pass, ruling out the build backend and provenance path. The generated sdist had five relative regular files, all 0644, no links/special entries; `data_filter` rejected none and changed only ownership fields to None. The exact rebuild and `COMMIT == "abc1234"` assertion remained green.

Test: the existing real-build integration test now carries a narrow pytest filterwarnings marker for this exact warning. Its final form was RED before the fix, was physically withheld from the fixer, then GREEN after repair. Removing only `filter="data"` returned it to RED; restoring the fix returned it to GREEN. It asserts observable warning/build/wheel behavior and survives internal refactors.

Fix: `TarFile.extractall(extracted, filter="data")`, matching Python’s safe future default, plus the exact warning-as-error regression guard. No production code, dependency, fixture, or existing provenance assertion changed.

Scope and safety: the call site is local to one test and has no caller that depends on implicit extraction, ownership restoration, or the warning. This restores forward-compatible test behavior, creates no product capability, adds no dependency, and weakens no test.

Siblings: a repository-wide `extractall(` sweep found no other omitted-filter instance. The four remaining sites use `data` or a stricter hardened filter. Parity sweep is N/A: this is a single test fixture, not a multi-channel product operation.

Residual risk and prevention: (accepted) CPython 3.11.0–3.11.3 predate the security backport for `filter=`; they are superseded patch levels, and `src/rebar/llm/workflow/snapshot.py:56-66` already refuses safe snapshot extraction there. (ticket filed) `fleeting-choosey-dore` owns the zizmor offline-mode warning. (ticket filed) `illegible-principal-grayfox` owns duplicate structured-output candidate warnings and carries an RP-01 coordination guard. Other full-suite warnings already have active owners: `ferrety-crippling-dairycow`, `stumpy-cinnabar-basenji`, and `dragonish-sylphic-sheep`.

Replication and gates: exact original command passed (1 passed); focused file passed (7 passed); `make lint` and `make typecheck` passed; `make test` passed with 13,527 passed, 60 skipped, 289 deselected. Local `rebar review-code` passed with zero findings. Gerrit 1833 received LLM-Review +1 and Verified +1 with zero comments, then merged as 81c3e9ec86d5fda18258e53e9fc9887d86251f45.
